text:
alex: Heads-up: I want to run a suite of synthetic traffic load tests tomorrow to validate our backpressure/admission-control thresholds for GPU pools. Goal is to catch queueing cascades before they hit customer routes.
maya: +1. Do you mean the dedicated GPU pools or hosted routing layer?
alex: Both. Start with a single dedicated pool in us-west-2 (small test pool) then exercise the routing layer to see global fallbacks. We need to validate: queue length growth vs configured queue_limit, 429 behavior, token-bucket rate limits per-pool, and cost burn at saturation.
ryan-oncall: Recommend test matrix: steady ramp to 80% GPU util, hold for 10m, then step to 95% util. Also one extreme spike to 150% request load to observe admission control enforcement.
tara: I'll own running locust. Proposed parameters: 50 workers, hatch rate 5/s, target RPS ~ 1200, per-request payloads that exercise decoding + KV cache hits. Sound good?
alex: Sounds good. For clarity: target per-GPU sustainable RPS baseline is ~200 reqs/s for the model variant we're using. We'll scale locust clients to exceed that.
maya: Don't forget region constraints: us-west GPU capacity reduced this week due to maintenance. Can we pin tests to a dedicated test pool instead of shared? Cost team will want an estimate.
alex: Using a dedicated test pool. Cost estimate: assume 4 GPUs for 60 minutes at p3/amax pricing -> ~ $xx (I'll sync with finance after we pick exact SKU). Also include a cheaper quantized variant test to see how backpressure differs.
ryan-oncall: Metrics to capture: per-pool queue_length, per-route 50/95/99 latencies, GPU_util, kernel_time, load_balancer 429 count, backend 5xx, and admission_controller_drops. Also export queue_age histogram.
tara: Will add probes to emit synthetic prefixes to test KV cache hits/misses. That affects tail latency a lot.
alex: We'll instrument two admission control configs. First: conservative token-bucket (rate=250/s, burst=100) + queue_limit=500. Second: strict circuit-breaker: if queue_length > 400 => immediate 429. We'll compare.
alex: Example admission config to apply to test front proxy (envoy filter):
```
filters:
  - name: envoy.filters.http.ratelimit
    typed_config:
      domain: "redwood-admit"
      rate_limit_service:
        grpc_service:
          envoy_grpc:
            cluster_name: "admit-service"
---
admission:
  token_bucket:
    rate: 250
    burst: 100
  queue_limit: 500
  drop_on_full: false
```
maya: For the circuit-breaker variant, drop_on_full=true and immediate 429. We'll want both in the tests.
ryan-oncall: Add a k8s job to generate load from inside cluster to avoid external LB artifacts. Use this to validate internal admission, bypass CDN caches.
alex: Good call. Tara can you schedule two jobs: internal-cluster-locust and external-e2e-locust? We want both vantage points.
tara: Yep. I'll schedule internal run at 09:00 PDT and external at 11:00 PDT tomorrow. I'll post the exact job IDs here.
deploy-bot: Created test cluster: redwood-loadtest-west-01 (4x-a100). kubeconfig uploaded to /infra/loadtests/kubeconfigs/west-01
infra-bot: Current baseline metrics for test pool (last 1h): gpu_util=22%, queue_length=0-3, avg_latency=78ms
alex: During the last small test we saw a queue slope increase: queue_length went from 10 -> 220 in 90s and 95p latency spiked to 4.2s. We need to see if admission control smooths that or just returns 429s.
ryan-oncall: If 429s spike it helps callers fail fast; better than increased latency for synchronous requesters. But for async retries we must ensure retry/backoff rules.
maya: Also watch cross-region routing: if us-west-2 gets many 429s, smart router retries to other regions and can cause cascading load elsewhere. We'll throttle retries at routing layer.
alex: Action items:
- tara: run locust jobs (internal + external) and attach raw logs (owner)
- ryan-oncall: add dashboard with queue_age, queue_length, admission_drops, regional_retry_count (owner)
- maya: confirm test pool capacity and cost estimate (owner)
- alex: stage the two admission configs and coordinate test execution (owner)
Please ping me in-thread when you start so we can correlate timestamps.

tara: Will do. Quick question: how long should we hold at target? You said 10m for 80% hold. For the spike test, hold 2m at peak?
alex: Yes: ramp 10m -> hold 10m -> spike 2m -> cooldown 5m. Repeat for circuit-breaker config.
ryan-oncall: Also include a long tail test: moderate load for 2h to check slow memory leaks or kernel slowdowns.
maya: FYI cost: 4 A100s for 2h ~ rough $X00 — finance flagged if we exceed 500% burn vs baseline, so keep single pool tests short.
tara: Understood. I'll post the run IDs and k6/locust logs here after each job completes.
alex: One more: capture GC/pagemap and OOM events from nvidia-smi and container logs. If we see memory thrashing, that indicates queuing at host-level not just at front proxy.
ryan-oncall: Add a short script to tail /var/log/nvidia-installer and container logs and push to the loadtest log bucket.

deploy-bot: Loadtest runner started: job/locust-internal-1743219001
maya: I'll watch routing metrics and temporarily disable cross-region fallback to avoid accidental traffic storms.

tara: locust-internal finished. quick summary: peak RPS 1.4k, gpu_util averaged 92% at peak, queue_length peaked 612, 95p latency 5.6s, admission_controller_drops=0 under token-bucket config
alex: Interesting — token-bucket allowed large queueing instead of dropping. That confirms we need queue_limit smaller or drop_on_full.
maya: circuit-breaker run next?
tara: circuit-breaker run done. summary: peak RPS 1.4k, queue_length capped ~405, admission_controller_drops=487 at peak, 95p latency 420ms, client 429s rose to 32% during spike.
alex: That's what we want to avoid tail latency risk. We need to ensure client SDKs handle 429s with exponential backoff and jitter.
ryan-oncall: Agreed. I'll create a short doc for the SDK teams with recommended retry rules: max_retries=3, base_backoff=100ms, max_backoff=2s, jitter=true.

maya: Postmortem note: when scaling to multi-region, circuit-breaker in one region may push retries to other regions. We should add a global retry budget and per-route backoff.
alex: Good point. We'll add a config for routing to cap cross-region retries per request.

tara: Uploading logs: s3://redwood-loadtests/1743214567/ (locust, metrics, nvidia logs)
alex: Thanks. Follow-ups: roll the conservative drop_on_full setting into a canary route for customer beta traffic next week, monitor for erroneous 429s. :thumbsup:

maya: +1
ryan-oncall: I'll own the canary dashboard and alerts for first 48h.

alex: Thanks everyone. Thread closed after we merge canary and confirm SDK retry rules.
